pages.title: File:Map of the Dzungar Khanate, in 1717.png

Credit.value:
Own work, Credits to User:पाटलिपुत्र for base of the map, as he uploaded under CC-BY-SA 4.0, and naturalearthdata.com, offered to the Public Domain


Sources: According to Ciuqin, the Dzungar Khanate had initially extended from the Irtysh to the Sali Mountains, and the Boke River. They later extended to the Ili River, they soon remained on the region north of Tian Shan, followed by Torghut–Dorbet migration to Volga, and the Khoshut migration to Qinghai.[1]

The Dzungars did not own the Western Bank of the Irtysh, as the Yesim Khan of the Kazakh Khanate had expulsed the Oirats from the Western Banks, during a civil war between Chokhur and Torobaikhu/Gushi Khan.[2]

Later, the Oirats expanded deep into the Altai Mountains, and the Yenisei during Sengge Chechen Khong Tayiji's rule, as the Dzungars annexed the Altan Khan of the Khalkhas, and vassalized the Kyrgyz people that resided in the Area.[3]

Soon the Dzungars expanded into the Biya, and Katun Rivers as they destroyed a Russian fortress between them, while they also ravaged Russian towns in the area.[4]

The Dzungars soon expanded southwards, as they conquered the Tarim Basin from 1679–1680,[5] and Tibet from 1717–1720.[6]
